chunks: Yunus narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him), 'Are the major sins excepted in that He forgives whom He wills?' He said: 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Are major sins unforgivable in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kāfī, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the category of major sins (al-kabāʾir) includes an implicit exception for divine pardon, countering the view that they incur eternal punishment. This highlights the Shia theological balance between the severity of major transgressions and the boundless scope of God's mercy, which can forgive whom He wills, provided repentance or divine grace intervenes.
